summary: Sustained p99 tail latency from batcher pacing jitter causing delayed flushes and intermittent 504s
description: Issue summary: ParcelAI reports sustained increases in p99 latency and occasional 504 gateway timeouts for generation requests routed through the hosted API. Impact: customer-facing latency regression starting 2026-03-13 15:20 UTC producing degraded UX for interactive flows and some API client timeouts. Timeline and detection: customer escalated to support; automated SLO alerts (p99 > 1s) triggered at ~15:24 UTC; support created this ticket at 15:40 UTC. Observed behavior: - Baseline before incident: p95 ~200-350ms, p99 ~420-550ms. - During incident: p95 ~600-900ms, p99 spikes 1.5s-3.2s; intermittent 504s at API gateway when request processing exceeded client timeout. - Spikes appear correlated with periods of mixed short/long sequence workloads and sustained QPS bursts. Expected behavior: p95/p99 within normal SLO bounds and no gateway 504s for steady QPS workloads. Impacted customers: ParcelAI production traffic; other customers in us-east saw minor transient effects.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send mixed-length generation workload to hosted API in us-east (mix of 16-token and 1024-token requests) at ~120 rps total from multiple connections.
2) Ensure continuous-batcher is enabled (default production config).
3) Observe p95/p99 with SLO dashboards or curl+timing - p99 should occasionally spike above 1.5s under these conditions.
4) Reproduce more reliably by interleaving short bursts of long requests every 10-30s to create heterogeneous batch composition.

comments: 2026-03-13 15:45 - Aisha Khan (Support): Customer reported UX regressions and provided sample request IDs; attached request IDs and SLO graphs. Asked engineering to triage batcher behavior.

2026-03-13 16:02 - Ethan Carter (SRE): Correlated SLO alerts with batcher flush events on worker-32; seeing unusually long flush delays (~1.2s) when batches contain mix of very short and very long sequences. Investigating pacing heuristic and timer drift.
2026-03-13 16:30 - ParcelAI (Customer): Confirms elevated latency around 15:20-16:00 UTC, sending additional trace IDs on three requests.

2026-03-13 17:10 - Ethan Carter (SRE): Applied temporary mitigation: route ParcelAI traffic to a pool with conservative batching (max_batch_wait_ms lowered) and increased API client timeout. Customer reports immediate improvement; p99 dropped below 700ms for routed traffic. Continuing root-cause analysis for platform-wide fix.
investigation_notes: Observation: Issue reproduces under heterogeneous sequence-length mixes. Continuous batcher waits for alignment windows leading to extended flush delays when long sequences enter the queue mid-window.
Hypothesis 1: Pacing heuristic combined with jitter in the worker's event loop causes the batch-flush timer to be extended beyond configured max_wait under certain alignment conditions.
Hypothesis 2: Interaction with KV-cache warmup: long requests trigger cache fills that delay subsequent callbacks, increasing event-loop latencies and delaying flush path.
Data points: Worker-32 has normal CPU/GPU utilization; network latencies low; but batcher flush-delay histogram shows heavy tail starting ~15:20 UTC. No memory pressure observed.
short_term_mitigation: Rerouted ParcelAI to a dedicated pool with max_batch_wait_ms reduced from 12ms -> 4ms for immediate relief.
Increased API gateway upstream timeout for the routed pool to 2500ms to avoid 504s during mitigation window.
Enabled request-level debug logging for affected worker nodes for 2 hours to capture more traces.
proposed_long_term_fix: Adjust batcher pacing heuristic to enforce strict max_wait (no implicit extension) and add defensive backstop that flushes if event-loop stalls exceed 200ms.
Add unit+integration tests simulating mixed short/long sequence workloads and event-loop jitter to prevent regressions.
Instrument KV-cache warmup path to measure callback latencies and decouple cache writes from batch flush-critical path where possible.
Rollout plan: code change -> staging canary (5% traffic) -> prod canary (25% 1h) -> full rollout if metrics stable.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation applied and verified for ParcelAI; customer confirmed improved UX by 16:40 UTC.
Engineering tracked suspicious change to batcher timer scheduling in PR #3241 (see related_github_prs). PR author is notified and follow-up fix branch created.
Full fix targeted for 2026-03-18; will include tests and configuration knobs.
next_steps: 1) Engineering to produce a patch enforcing strict max_wait semantics and backstop flush; link to dev branch and PR once created.
2) Run canary on staging then prod per rollout plan; monitor p95/p99, batch flush-delay histogram, and gateway 504 rate.
3) Postmortem to be drafted in Confluence including RCA and regression tests; assign owner for follow-up.
final_resolution: Mitigation in place for customer (routing + timeout) and engineering working on code-level fix. Ticket will be updated with PR/rollout status; awaiting deployment to staging for validation.
